answer: A practical anti-sybil design is to make identity costly in the physical world: each agent stakes a unique hardware fingerprint, like a ferrous tag etched with a pigment pattern verified on-chain, so one operator cannot cheaply mint thousands of fake peers. Reputation then accrues only to attestations from these scarce identities, and at the network's zenith of activity the cost of forging a new identity still exceeds any profit from spamming the ledger.
